title: Clean Occurrence Data
text:
What this script does
Clean and standardize herbarium specimen records previously downloaded from biodiversity databases.The workflow uses the barRoso package, which standardizes biodiversity occurrence datasets and flags common issues such as duplicates, missing identifications, and problematic collections.

title: Clean Occurrence Data
text:
Setup
Load the R packages required for taxonomic and dataset standardization.

#install.packages("devtools")

# LCVP: https://github.com/idiv-biodiversity/LCVP
#devtools::install_github("idiv-biodiversity/LCVP")
library(LCVP)

# lcvplants: https://github.com/idiv-biodiversity/lcvplants
#devtools::install_github("idiv-biodiversity/lcvplants")
library(lcvplants)

# barRoso: https://github.com/DBOSlab/barRoso
#devtools::install_github("DBOSlab/barRoso")
library(barRoso)

Load general packages to operate data frames and export to Excel.

#install.packages(dplyr)
library(dplyr)

#install.packages(openxlsx)
library(openxlsx)

Load auxiliary functions for the script.

source("functions/auxiliary_functions.R")

Load the merged dataset generated in the previous step of the pipeline, if it is not already present in the R environment.

all_data <- read.xlsx("output_data/")

Create folders in the directory to save the occurrence data:

if (!dir.exists("output_data/")) dir.create("output_data/", recursive = TRUE)

timestamp_tag <- format(Sys.time(), "%d%b%Y")
clean_data_path <- file.path("output_data/", paste0("clean_data_",  timestamp_tag, ".xlsx"))

title: Clean Occurrence Data
text:
Harmonize dataset structure
Convert country names to standard English format using a auxiliary function.

if ("country" %in% names(all_data)) {
  all_data$country <- convert_country_EN(all_data$country)
}

Different biodiversity databases provide slightly different field structures.The following step harmonizes the dataset structure by selecting relevant fields and inserting missing columns.

cols <- c(names(data_reflora))

cols <- insert_after_word(cols, c(
  basisOfRecord = "gbifID",
  stateProvince = "county",
  scientificName = "acceptedScientificName",
  maximumElevationInMeters = "elevation",
  identificationRemarks = "vernacularName",
  identificationRemarks = "eventRemarks",
  fieldNotes = "habitat",
  day = "lifeStage",
  catalogNumber = "barcode"
))

all_data <- all_data %>%
  select(any_of(cols)) %>%
  filter(basisOfRecord %in% c("PRESERVED_SPECIMEN", "Preservedspecimen"))

title: Clean Occurrence Data
text:
Clean the dataset
The barroso_std() function performs several cleaning and validation procedures for herbarium occurrence datasets. These procedures are controlled by function arguments and can be enabled depending on the user’s objectives.
In this example, the function:

Flags possible misidentifications (flag_missid)
Detects duplicate specimens (flag_duplicates)
Removes duplicated records (rm_duplicates)
Identifies unvouchered records (unvouchered)
Removes problematic collections (delunkcoll)

Additional arguments and options can be explored in the function documentation using ?barroso_std().

clean_data <- barRoso::barroso_std(
  all_data,
  unvouchered = TRUE,
  delunkcoll = TRUE,
  flag_missid = TRUE,
  flag_duplicates = TRUE,
  rm_duplicates = TRUE,
  rm_original_column = TRUE
)

title: Clean Occurrence Data
text:
Export the cleaned dataset
Export the cleaned dataset to Excel for manual inspection and correction.

openxlsx::write.xlsx(clean_data, file = clean_data_path)
}

title: Clean Occurrence Data
section: Reload the dataset after manual corrections (optional)
text:
Reload the dataset after manual corrections (optional)
You may need to make manual corrections on the formatting of the collector names, for example. If needed, the barroso_std() function can be executed again after manual edits to ensure the dataset remains standardized.

clean_data <- read.xlsx("output_data/clean_data_20260112_160824.xlsx")

title: Add morphological traits
text:
What this script does
Generate a morphological trait matrix associated with the curated species occurrence dataset produced in previous steps of the pipeline.
The workflow uses the morph_add_traits() function of the moRphoTaxa package, which generates a standardized matrix of qualitative and quantitative morphological traits. The resulting dataset can include general traits shared across angiosperms as well as traits specific to selected plant groups — angiosperm families and, for non-angiosperm lineages (mosses, lycophytes, ferns and conifers), higher-rank groups.
The final dataset can be exported as an Excel file for data entry and morphometric analyses.

title: Add morphological traits
text:
Setup
Load the moRphoTaxa package, required to create and export data frames.

# moRphoTaxa: https://dboslab.github.io/moRphoTaxa-website/
#devtools::install_github("DBOSlab/moRphoTaxa")
library(moRphoTaxa)

If the curated occurrence dataset from the previous steps is not loaded in the R environment, it can be imported and used as the base data frame for the trait dataset. Otherwise, the workflow generates a trait matrix without associated species records.

clean_data <- read.xlsx("output_data/")

Create a folder to store the resulting dataset, and define the file path that will be passed to morph_add_traits() via file_name.

if (!dir.exists("output_data/")) dir.create("output_data/", recursive = TRUE)

timestamp_tag <- format(Sys.time(), "%d%b%Y")
trait_data_path <- file.path("output_data/", paste0("trait_data_",  timestamp_tag, ".xlsx"))

title: Add morphological traits
text:
Inspect available traits (optional)
traits_database is a reference data frame bundled with the package, listing every qualitative and quantitative trait currently implemented — including its full name, abbreviated code, trait type, and the trait set (trait_scope) it belongs to. Inspecting it before running morph_add_traits() helps decide which default and taxon-specific traits to request.

data(traits_database)

# available trait sets
unique(traits_database$trait_scope)

# traits for a given group, e.g. Passifloraceae
subset(traits_database, trait_scope == "passifloraceae")

title: Add morphological traits
text:
morph_add_traits()
The morph_add_traits() function creates a data frame containing morphological traits and optionally associates them with an occurrence dataset.
The traits included in the dataset are controlled through function arguments:

base_df
A data frame containing species occurrence records. If NULL, the function creates only the trait matrix without associating it with occurrence data.


trait_name
Defines how trait columns are labeled:

"trait full name" → descriptive trait names

"trait code" → abbreviated trait codes

"both" → full name and code combined



quali_default and quanti_default
Logical arguments controlling whether the default qualitative and quantitative traits commonly used across angiosperms are included. Both are automatically switched to FALSE when quali_specific/quanti_specific refers to a non-angiosperm group ("bryophyta" or "polipodiopsida"), since the angiosperm default traits (corolla, calyx, fruit, seed, etc.) do not apply to those lineages. A message is printed when this happens, unless the argument was already set to FALSE or verbose = FALSE.


quali_specific and quanti_specific
Character arguments used to add taxon-specific traits. Currently available presets include:

"asteraceae"
"bryophyta"
"cactaceae"
"caesalpinioidae"
"orchidaceae"
"papilionoideae"
"passifloraceae"
"polipodiopsida"

If NULL, only the default traits will be returned.


save
Logical argument controlling whether the resulting dataset is exported as an Excel file.


file_name
Character string with the file path (including file name and .xlsx extension) used to save the resulting data frame when save = TRUE. If NULL, a file is saved automatically inside output_data/, with a name generated from the current date and time. Ignored when save = FALSE.


verbose
Logical argument controlling whether informative messages are printed during execution, including the location of exported files and any automatic quali_default/quanti_default adjustments for non-angiosperm presets.

title: Add morphological traits
section: Add morphological traits to the dataset
text:
Add morphological traits to the dataset
In this example, the function:

Creates a morphological trait dataset

Includes the default qualitative and quantitative traits

Adds traits specific to Papilionoideae (Leguminosae)

Exports the dataset as an Excel file at the path defined above

Users should modify the function arguments according to their needs (e.g., selecting different trait sets or plant groups).

df_morph_traits <- morph_add_traits(base_df = NULL,
                                    trait_name = "both",
                                    quali_default = TRUE,
                                    quanti_default = TRUE,
                                    quali_specific = "papilionoideae",
                                    quanti_specific = "papilionoideae",
                                    save = TRUE,
                                    file_name = trait_data_path,
                                    verbose = TRUE)

The output of the function is a data frame containing the original occurrence data (if provided) along with columns for the selected morphological traits; the dataset is also exported as an Excel file at trait_data_path, allowing manual insertion of trait values.






Note



For a non-angiosperm dataset (e.g. mosses), requesting the corresponding preset directly disables the angiosperm defaults:

df_morph_traits_moss <- morph_add_traits(base_df = NULL,
                                         trait_name = "both",
                                         quali_specific = "bryophyta",
                                         quanti_specific = "bryophyta",
                                         save = TRUE,
                                         file_name = "output_data/trait_data_bryophyta.xlsx")

title: Get Herbarium Data
text:
What this script does
Download herbarium specimen records from four biodiversity databases:

speciesLink

REFLORA

GBIF

The records are merged into a single dataset and exported as an Excel file.

text:
Setup

title: Get Herbarium Data
text:
speciesLink
Download records from speciesLink. This function requires a personal API key to download the data. You can generate one at:
https://specieslink.net/aut/profile/apikeys

#Example:

personal_key <- "DBpBRprOuNV8ZWoxRFcr"

To query multiple species, the function downloads a separate dataset for each species in the list.

data_speciesLink <- lapply(
  targeted_taxa,
  function(x) plantR::rspeciesLink(
    dir = "input_data/",
    filename = "spLink_records_search",
    save = TRUE,
    key = personal_key,
    basisOfRecord = NULL,
    family = NULL,
    species = x,
    collectionCode = NULL,
    country = NULL,
    stateProvince = NULL,
    county = NULL,
    Coordinates = NULL,
    CoordinatesQuality = NULL,
    Scope = NULL,
    Synonyms = "no synomyms",
    Typus = FALSE,
    Images = FALSE,
    RedList = NULL,
    MaxRecords = 5000,
    file.format = "csv",
    compress = FALSE
  )
)

Next, the resulting data frames are combined into a single dataset.

# Adding species names to each element of the list
names(data_speciesLink) <- targeted_taxa

# Binding all searchs and keeping a column with the named used in the search
data_speciesLink <- dplyr::bind_rows(data_speciesLink, .id = "original_search")

Finally, an auxiliary function standardizes the column names to conform to Darwin Core terminology.

data_speciesLink <- fix_column_names(data_speciesLink)

title: Get Herbarium Data
text:
REFLORA
Download specimen records from the REFLORA Virtual Herbarium.

data_reflora <- refloraR::reflora_records(
  herbarium = NULL,
  repatriated = TRUE,
  taxon = targeted_taxa,
  state = NULL,
  recordYear = NULL,
  indets = TRUE,
  reorder = c("herbarium", "taxa", "collector", "area", "year"),
  path = NULL,
  updates = TRUE,
  verbose = TRUE,
  save = FALSE,
  dir = "input_data/",
  filename = "reflora_records_search"
)

The REFLORA package temporarily stores individual downloaded records in a local directory. Since the records are already loaded into the data_reflora data frame, the temporary folder is removed to keep the workspace clean.

unlink("reflora_download/", recursive = TRUE, force = TRUE)

title: Get Herbarium Data
text:
JABOT
Download specimen records from the JABOT database of the Rio de Janeiro Botanical Garden.

data_jabot <- jabotR::jabot_records(
  herbarium = NULL,
  taxon = targeted_taxa,
  state = NULL,
  recordYear = NULL,
  indets = TRUE,
  reorder = c("herbarium", "taxa", "collector", "area", "year"),
  path = NULL,
  updates = TRUE,
  verbose = TRUE,
  save = FALSE,
  dir = "input_data/",
  filename = "jabot_records_search"
)

As in the REFLORA step, the temporary download directory is removed because the records are already stored in the data_jabot data frame.

unlink("jabot_download/", recursive = TRUE, force = TRUE)

title: Get Herbarium Data
text:
GBIF
Download occurrence records from the Global Biodiversity Information Facility (GBIF). As in the speciesLink query, the function downloads a separate dataset for each species in the list in a multi species search.

data_gbif <- lapply(
  targeted_taxa,
  function(x) plantR::rgbif2(
    dir = "input_data/",
    filename = "gbif_records_search",
    species = x,
    n.records = 5000,
    force = TRUE,
    remove_na = FALSE,
    save = FALSE,
    file.format = "csv",
    compress = FALSE
  )
)

The resulting data frames are then combined into a single dataset.

# Adding species names to each element of the list
names(data_gbif) <- targeted_taxa

# Binding all searchs and keeping a column with the named used in the search
data_gbif <- dplyr::bind_rows(data_gbif, .id = "original_search")

title: Get Herbarium Data
text:
Merge all sources
First, add a column identifying the origin of each record.

data_gbif$source <- "GBIF"
data_jabot$source <- "JABOT"
data_reflora$source <- "REFLORA"
data_speciesLink$source <- "speciesLink"

Then convert all fields to character before merging.

data_list <- list(data_gbif, data_jabot, data_reflora, data_speciesLink)

data_list <- lapply(data_list, function(df) {
  df %>% dplyr::mutate(across(everything(), as.character))
})

Combine the sources.

all_data <- dplyr::bind_rows(data_list)

title: Run analysis
text:
What this script does
Runs the full downstream analysis on a curated morphological + occurrence dataset using the moRphoTaxa package: builds the morphometric and ecogeographic matrices, checks data quality, explores structure through ordination and clustering, tests group differences with confirmatory statistics, and closes with an environmental/niche analysis based on WorldClim and SoilGrids variables.
Most analysis functions share a small set of conventions:

A *_blocks argument selects which trait block(s) to analyze — "veg" (vegetative), "flo" (floral), "fru" (fruit), or "all". Blocks are defined by the veg_first/flo_first/fru_first boundaries set in morph_matrix_setting().
file_formats controls which image format(s) each function saves its plots in (e.g. "jpeg", "pdf", or c("pdf", "jpeg")).
verbose controls whether the function prints progress/status messages, including the location of saved files.
save_xlsx (where available) controls whether numeric results are additionally exported to an Excel workbook alongside the plots.

title: Run analysis
text:
Setup

# moRphoTaxa: https://dboslab.github.io/moRphoTaxa-website/
#devtools::install_github("DBOSlab/moRphoTaxa")
library(moRphoTaxa)


morph_matrix_setting()
Reads the curated dataset (an Excel file with one row per specimen/occurrence and one taxon column) and builds the standardized morphometric matrix used by every morph_*() function downstream. It also stores the vegetative/floral/fruit block boundaries as attributes so subsequent functions know which columns belong to which block.

morphmatrix <- morph_matrix_setting(xlsx_path = "output_data/all_data.xlsx",
                                    taxon_col = "taxon",
                                    species_selected = NULL,
                                    trait_name_type = "code",
                                    veg_first = "petiole_length/PETIlng",
                                    flo_first = "inflorescence_length/INFLlng",
                                    fru_first = "fruit_stipe_length/FRSTlng",
                                    colors = NULL)


xlsx_path — path to the source Excel file.
taxon_col — name of the column identifying taxa/groups.
species_selected — optional character vector to restrict the matrix to specific taxa; NULL keeps all of them.
trait_name_type — whether trait columns in the source file are labeled by "code", full name, or both (must match how the file was produced, e.g. by morph_add_traits()).
veg_first, flo_first, fru_first — the first column of each block (vegetative, floral, fruit), used to split the trait matrix into the "veg"/"flo"/"fru" blocks referenced everywhere else in the pipeline.
colors — optional named vector assigning a color to each taxon; if NULL, colors are generated automatically and stored as a taxon_colors attribute reused by every plotting function below.

title: Run analysis
text:
Data quality & exploration

morph_normality()
Tests each quantitative trait for normality (per block) and optionally produces Q-Q plots.

morph_normality(analysis_data = morphmatrix,
                norm_alpha = 0.05,
                norm_qq = TRUE,
                file_formats = "jpeg",
                verbose = TRUE)


norm_alpha — significance threshold for the normality test.
norm_qq — whether to also produce Q-Q plots for each trait.



morph_boxplots()
Draws boxplots (or violin plots) of each trait by taxon, for visual comparison across groups.

morph_boxplots(analysis_data = morphmatrix,
               plot_type = "violin",
               show_jitter = TRUE,
               min_n_total = 10,
               file_formats = "jpeg",
               verbose = TRUE)


plot_type — "boxplot" or "violin".
show_jitter — overlay individual data points as jitter.
min_n_total — minimum total sample size for a trait to be plotted.



morph_similarity()
Computes pairwise trait-to-trait correlations within each block and flags significant associations after multiple-testing correction.

morph_similarity(analysis_data = morphmatrix,
                 sim_blocks = "all",
                 sim_method = "pearson",
                 sim_p_adjust = "BH",
                 sim_alpha = 0.05,
                 sim_min_n = 5,
                 sim_pairs = NULL
                 file_formats = "jpeg")


sim_method — correlation method (e.g. "pearson", "spearman").
sim_p_adjust — p-value adjustment method ("BH" = Benjamini–Hochberg).
sim_min_n — minimum pairwise sample size for a trait pair to be included.
sim_pairs — list of character vectors of length two to produce an scatter plot

title: Run analysis
text:
Ordination

morph_pca()
Principal Component Analysis of the (quantitative) traits in each block, highlighting the top-contributing traits per axis.

morph_pca(analysis_data = morphmatrix,
          pca_blocks = "all",
          top_contrib = 10,
          file_formats = "jpeg",
          verbose = TRUE)


top_contrib — number of top-contributing traits reported/highlighted per component.



morph_pcoa()
Principal Coordinates Analysis on a dissimilarity matrix (default Gower, which handles mixed qualitative/quantitative traits), with an eigenvalue-correction method for negative eigenvalues.

morph_pcoa(analysis_data = morphmatrix,
           pcoa_blocks = "all",
           dist_method = "gower",
           correction = "lingoes",
           top_vars = 10,
           file_formats = "jpeg",
           verbose = TRUE)


dist_method — dissimilarity metric (e.g. "gower", "bray").
correction — negative-eigenvalue correction (e.g. "lingoes", "cailliez").
top_vars — number of top-contributing variables reported.



morph_nmds()
Non-metric multidimensional scaling, an alternative rank-based ordination.

morph_nmds(analysis_data = morphmatrix,
           nmds_blocks = "all",
           nmds_dist = "gower",
           nmds_k = 2,
           nmds_trymax = 100,
           nmds_seed = 42,
           file_formats = "jpeg",
           verbose = TRUE)


nmds_dist — distance method.
nmds_k — number of NMDS dimensions.
nmds_trymax — maximum number of random starts to find a stable solution.
nmds_seed — random seed, for reproducibility.

title: Run analysis
text:
Clustering

morph_dendrogram()
Hierarchical clustering (agglomerative), with a candidate linkage method and a search over the number of clusters up to k_max.

morph_dendrogram(analysis_data = morphmatrix,
                 dendro_blocks = "all",
                 dist_method = "bray",
                 linkage_candidates = "complete",
                 k_max = 8,
                 cluster_cols = NULL,
                 file_formats = c("pdf", "jpeg"),
                 verbose = TRUE)


linkage_candidates — linkage method(s) to evaluate (e.g. "complete", "average", "ward.D2").
k_max — upper bound on the number of clusters considered when cutting the tree.
cluster_cols — vector of colors used for dendrogram branches



morph_kmeans()
K-means partitioning, with a bootstrap procedure (kmeans_B) to help choose the number of clusters, visualized on the PCA axes produced by morph_pca().

morph_kmeans(analysis_data = morphmatrix,
             kmeans_blocks = "all",
             kmeans_k_max = 10,
             kmeans_B = 50,
             kmeans_nstart = 25,
             kmeans_pcs = c("PC1", "PC2"),
             kmeans_seed = 123,
             file_formats = "jpeg",
             verbose = TRUE)


kmeans_k_max — maximum number of clusters evaluated.
kmeans_B — number of bootstrap replicates used to assess cluster stability.
kmeans_nstart — number of random starts per k-means run (best solution kept).
kmeans_pcs — which PCA axes to plot the resulting clusters on.



morph_nmm()
Normal mixture-model clustering (via mclust), selecting the top contributing traits and drawing confidence ellipses per component.

morph_nmm(analysis_data = morphmatrix,
          nmm_blocks = "all",
          nmm_top_traits = 10,
          nmm_min_n = 10,
          ellipse_level = 0.4,
          nmm_seed = 123,
          save_xlsx = TRUE,
          file_formats = "jpeg",
          verbose = TRUE)


nmm_top_traits — number of traits used to fit/display the mixture model.
nmm_min_n — minimum sample size required to fit the model.
ellipse_level — confidence level of the plotted ellipses.

title: Run analysis
text:
Confirmatory

morph_anova()
One-way ANOVA of each quantitative trait by group, with multiple-testing correction.

morph_anova(analysis_data = morphmatrix,
            anova_blocks = "all",
            anova_groups = "taxon",
            anova_p_adjust = "BH",
            anova_alpha = 0.05,
            save_xlsx = TRUE,
            file_formats = "jpeg",
            verbose = TRUE)


anova_groups — grouping column used to test differences (typically taxon_col).



morph_permanova()
Permutational MANOVA on a dissimilarity matrix (default Gower), testing whether groups differ multivariately, with confidence ellipses on the ordination plot.

morph_permanova(analysis_data = morphmatrix,
                permanova_blocks = "all",
                dist_method = "gower",
                permutations = 999,
                min_n = 3,
                p_adjust = "BH",
                ellipse_level = 0.95,
                seed = 123,
                save_xlsx = TRUE,
                file_formats = "jpeg",
                verbose = TRUE)


permutations — number of permutations used to build the null distribution.
min_n — minimum group size to be included in the test.



morph_kruskal()
Non-parametric alternative to morph_anova(): Kruskal–Wallis test per trait, with optional Dunn’s post-hoc pairwise comparisons.

morph_kruskal(analysis_data = morphmatrix,
              kw_blocks = "all",
              kw_groups = "taxon",
              kw_p_adjust = "BH",
              kw_alpha = 0.05,
              kw_posthoc = TRUE,
              save_xlsx = TRUE,
              file_formats = "jpeg",
              verbose = TRUE)


kw_posthoc — whether to run Dunn’s post-hoc test when the omnibus test is significant.



morph_lda()
Linear Discriminant Analysis (MASS::lda), plotted on the requested discriminant axes with confidence ellipses; missing values can be imputed before fitting.

morph_lda(analysis_data = morphmatrix,
          lda_blocks = "all",
          lda_group = "taxon",
          lda_lds = c("LD1", "LD2"),
          lda_ellipse = 0.95,
          lda_min_n = 3,
          lda_impute = "mean",
          save_xlsx = TRUE,
          file_formats = "jpeg",
          verbose = TRUE)


lda_lds — which discriminant axes to plot.
lda_impute — imputation strategy for missing trait values (e.g. "mean", or "none"/NULL to drop incomplete cases, depending on the implementation).



morph_cva()
Canonical Variate Analysis, a group-mean-based alternative/complement to LDA for exploring shape/trait divergence among taxa.

morph_cva(analysis_data = morphmatrix,
          cva_blocks = "all",
          cva_ellipse = 0.95,
          cva_min_n = 3,
          file_formats = c("pdf", "jpeg"),
          verbose = TRUE)


cva_ellipse — confidence level of the plotted group ellipses.
cva_min_n — minimum group size to be included.



morph_dapc()
Discriminant Analysis of Principal Components — combines a PCA dimensionality-reduction step with LDA, useful when traits are highly correlated or numerous relative to sample size.

morph_dapc(analysis_data = morphmatrix,
           dapc_blocks = "all",
           dapc_min_n = 3,
           dapc_ellipse = 0.95,
           file_formats = "jpeg",
           verbose = TRUE)


dapc_min_n — minimum group size to be included.

title: Run analysis
text:
Environmental & niche analysis

geo_matrix_setting()
Builds the ecogeographic counterpart of morph_matrix_setting(): pulls WorldClim bioclimatic variables for each occurrence record (always) and, optionally, SoilGrids edaphic variables, returning a matrix analogous in structure to the morphometric one.

geomatrix <- geo_matrix_setting(xlsx_path = "output_data/all_data.xlsx",
                                sheet = 1,
                                taxon_col = "taxon",
                                species_selected = NULL,
                                wc_res = 2.5,
                                edaphic = TRUE,
                                edaphic_vars = c("clay", "sand", "silt", "soc",
                                                 "phh2o", "cec", "nitrogen",
                                                 "bdod", "cfvo", "ocd", "ocs"),
                                edaphic_depth = 5,
                                data_path = "variables_data/",
                                verbose = TRUE)


sheet — sheet of xlsx_path to read, when the file has more than one.
wc_res — WorldClim spatial resolution, in arc-minutes (e.g. 2.5).
edaphic — whether to also fetch SoilGrids edaphic variables; when FALSE, only climate variables are used.
edaphic_vars — which SoilGrids variables to fetch (clay/sand/silt fractions, organic carbon, pH, CEC, nitrogen, bulk density, coarse fragments, organic carbon density/stock).
edaphic_depth — soil depth (cm) at which the edaphic variables are sampled.
data_path — folder where the downloaded/cached raster layers are stored.



geo_bioclim_exploratory()
Ranks the 19 bioclimatic variables by variance and pairwise correlation, and summarizes them with a PCA, exporting the ranking to Excel.

geo_bioclim_exploratory(geodata = geomatrix,
                        bio_x = 15,
                        bio_y = 12,
                        cor_threshold = 0.8,
                        file_formats = "jpg",
                        verbose = TRUE)


bio_x, bio_y — which two bioclimatic variables (by BIO code number) to use for the pairwise scatter/dispersion plot.
cor_threshold — correlation cutoff above which a variable pair is flagged as redundant.



geo_bioclim_maps()
Maps a chosen bioclimatic layer across the study area, together with occurrence points, with optional country/state borders and rivers.

geo_bioclim_maps(geodata = geomatrix,
                 bio_map_layer = 12,
                 bio_x = 1,
                 bio_y = 12,
                 show_country_states = NULL,
                 show_rivers = FALSE,
                 river_scale = 10,
                 inset = TRUE,
                 pt_shapes = NULL,
                 save = TRUE,
                 file_formats = "jpg",
                 verbose = TRUE)


bio_map_layer — bioclimatic variable plotted as the background raster.
show_country_states — optional vector of country/state names to outline.
inset — whether to add a locator inset map.
pt_shapes — optional per-taxon point shapes for the occurrence markers.



geo_morph_mantel()
Mantel test comparing geographic distance to morphological (trait) distance, to check for isolation-by-distance-like patterns.

geo_morph_mantel(geodata = geomatrix,
                 analysis_data = morphmatrix,
                 cor_method = "pearson",
                 permutations = 999,
                 dist_method = "gower",
                 geo_dist_method = "euclidean",
                 file_formats = "jpg",
                 verbose = TRUE)


dist_method — dissimilarity metric for the morphological distance matrix.
geo_dist_method — distance metric for geographic coordinates.



morph_autocorrelation()
Tests each trait for lag-1 spatial autocorrelation along an ordering of the specimens (by latitude, longitude, or original row order), producing per-block plots and a summary table.

morph_autocorrelation(analysis_data = morphmatrix,
                      geodata = geomatrix,
                      blocks = "all",
                      cor_method = "pearson",
                      order_by = "latitude",
                      file_formats = "jpg",
                      verbose = TRUE)


order_by — how specimens are ordered before computing the lag-1 autocorrelation: "latitude", "longitude", or "none" (keeps original row order).



geo_morph_rda()
Redundancy Analysis constraining morphological traits by bioclimatic variables, run per trait block, after dropping redundant environmental variables above a correlation threshold.

geo_morph_rda(analysis_data = morphmatrix,
              geodata = geomatrix,
              blocks = "all",
              env_vars = NULL,
              permutations = 999,
              scale_data = TRUE,
              env_cor_threshold = 0.95,
              file_formats = "jpg",
              verbose = TRUE)


env_vars — environmental variables to use as constraints; NULL auto-selects all bio* columns.
scale_data — whether to standardize morphological and environmental data before fitting.
env_cor_threshold — correlation cutoff above which redundant environmental variables are dropped before the analysis.



geo_enm()
Ecological Niche Modelling: fits a presence/background model per taxon (with a spatial buffer, cross-validation folds, and permutation-based variable importance), optionally mapped with country/state borders.

geo_enm(geodata = geomatrix,
        buffer_km = 100,
        pa_ratio = 2,
        folds = 5,
        min_occ = 3,
        importance_perm = 10,
        seed = 123,
        show_country_states = NULL,
        inset = TRUE,
        save = TRUE,
        file_formats = "jpg",
        verbose = TRUE)


buffer_km — radius (km) around occurrences used to define the background/pseudo-absence area.
pa_ratio — ratio of background/pseudo-absence points to presence points.
folds — number of cross-validation folds.
min_occ — minimum number of occurrences required to model a taxon.
importance_perm — number of permutations used to estimate variable importance.



geo_niche_overlap()
Quantifies niche overlap between taxa in environmental space (e.g. Schoener’s D-type metrics), with a similarity/equivalence test based on randomization.

geo_niche_overlap(geodata = geomatrix,
                  var_threshold = 0.95,
                  cor_cutoff = 0.8,
                  grid_size = 100,
                  iterations = 1000,
                  alpha = 0.05,
                  min_occ = 3,
                  n_cores = 1,
                  seed = 123,
                  save = TRUE,
                  file_formats = "jpg",
                  verbose = TRUE)


var_threshold — variance-explained threshold used when reducing environmental variables (e.g. via PCA) before building the niche space.
cor_cutoff — correlation cutoff for dropping redundant environmental variables.
grid_size — resolution of the environmental-space grid used to estimate niche overlap.
iterations — number of randomizations for the overlap significance test.
n_cores — number of cores used for parallel computation.

title: moRphoTaxa
text:
What this pipeline does
moRphoTaxa operationalizes integrative morphometric taxonomy within a fully reproducible R framework, combining the moRphoTaxa package’s functions with a scripted pipeline that chains them together. The pipeline executes the complete analytical workflow, from large-scale herbarium data acquisition and standardized occurrence-data harmonization to automated trait-matrix construction, multivariate morphometric inference, and bioclimatic-space analysis, enabling objective detection of phenetic structure, statistically supported morphogroups, and environmentally structured lineages within a unified analytical system.
The pipeline performs:

Automated herbarium record acquisition from multiple repositories

Standardized harmonization of occurrence datasets

Scripted generation of morphometric matrix presets, via moRphoTaxa functions such as morph_add_traits()
Multivariate morphometric analyses (e.g., PCA, clustering), via moRphoTaxa functions such as morph_pca() and morph_kmeans()
Bioclimatic-space extraction and ordination (e.g., NMDS), via moRphoTaxa functions such as geo_matrix_setting() and morph_nmds()
Generation of reproducible analytical outputs

title: moRphoTaxa
text:
Why this pipeline exists
Species delimitation in recently diverged lineages and species complexes is often constrained by:

Overlapping morphological characters

Weak or multidimensional phenetic structure

Partial ecological divergence

Despite the availability of large herbarium datasets, workflows for integrative morphometrics remain fragmented, manually assembled, and difficult to reproduce. moRphoTaxa addresses this limitation by providing a standardized, scripted analytical infrastructure — an R package of documented functions plus the pipeline that sequences them — that connects specimen-based data to quantitative inference in a transparent, repeatable and scalable manner.

title: moRphoTaxa
text:
Design Principles
moRphoTaxa was built around five core principles:

Reproducibility — fully scripted and version-controlled workflow, backed by a documented, exported R package

Transparency — traceable transformation from raw data to inference

Modularity — independent yet interoperable components, each corresponding to one or more moRphoTaxa functions

Transferability — adaptable across plant families

Scalability — suitable for megadiverse systems

title: moRphoTaxa
text:
Core Workflow
The pipeline is organized into four integrated modules, each drawing on a dedicated set of moRphoTaxa package functions:

title: moRphoTaxa
text:
Getting Started
To run moRphoTaxa:

Install the moRphoTaxa package (e.g., devtools::install_github("DBOSlab/moRphoTaxa")) — the pipeline calls its functions at every step.
Navigate through the sections corresponding to each pipeline module.

Carefully read the instructions and methodological notes provided in each page.

Copy and execute the R code blocks directly in your R environment (RStudio recommended).

Follow the workflow sequentially, as later modules depend on outputs generated in previous steps.

Each stage of the pipeline is documented using executable Quarto files. The complete project archive, including all scripts, functions, templates, and example datasets, will be publicly available on the project’s GitHub repository, enabling version control, reuse, and long-term accessibility.

title: morph_autocorrelation
text:
moRphoTaxa::morph_autocorrelation()


Description
Measures, for each morphological trait, how similar the values of neighbouring specimens are when specimens are ordered along a geographic axis (latitude or longitude) or kept in their original spreadsheet order. A positive lag-1 autocorrelation indicates that specimens close to each other in the ordering tend to have similar values (a gradient or geographic structure in the trait), a value near zero indicates no ordering-related structure, and a negative value indicates that neighbouring specimens tend to alternate.
Takes the morphometric matrix produced by morph_matrix_setting() and, when specimens are ordered by geography, the geographical matrix produced by geo_matrix_setting(). For each requested trait block, the function computes the autocorrelation of every trait, draws a ranked bar chart, and writes a combined summary table.


Details
Ordering specimens. Specimens are matched by row names (the specimen identifiers shared by morph_matrix_setting() and geo_matrix_setting()) and sorted once, before any block is analyzed:

"latitude" (default): ascending decimalLatitude;
"longitude": ascending decimalLongitude;
"none": the row order of analysis_data is kept (the spreadsheet order, e.g. collection number). geodata is not needed in this case.

When ordering by latitude or longitude, specimens of analysis_data that are absent from geodata (or have a missing coordinate) are dropped. Specimens with identical coordinates keep their relative spreadsheet order.
Lag-1 autocorrelation. For each trait, the specimens are taken in the chosen order and the trait value of each specimen is correlated with the value of the preceding specimen, using the coefficient given by cor_method. A pair of consecutive specimens is used only if both have a measured value for that trait; the autocorrelation is NA, and the trait is left out of the results, when fewer than 3 such pairs exist or when the trait is constant among them. The coefficient is descriptive: no significance test is performed. It only detects structure along the chosen ordering axis.
Pooled taxa. All specimens in analysis_data are ordered together. If several taxa are included and they occupy different parts of the ordering axis, differences between taxa contribute to the autocorrelation. To examine geographic structure within a single taxon, build analysis_data with species_selected set to that taxon in morph_matrix_setting().
Trait blocks. The vegetative ("veg"), floral ("flo"), and fruit ("fru") trait blocks are read from the "base_cols" attribute of analysis_data, created by morph_matrix_setting(). With blocks = "all", each available block is run, followed by every combination of two or more available blocks, named by concatenating the block names ("vegflo", "vegfru", "flofru", "vegflofru"). Any single block or combination can also be requested by name. Because the autocorrelation is computed trait by trait, a trait has the same value in every block that contains it; combined blocks only group traits in a single chart and table.
Outputs. One chart per block (Autocorrelation_<block>.<ext>) and a single Autocorrelation_summary.csv with all blocks are written to a dated subfolder (format(Sys.time(), "%d%b%Y")) inside "Figs_Autocorrelation". The dated subfolder means repeated runs do not overwrite each other. Trait labels in the charts and the summary are the descriptive part of the column name, with underscores replaced by spaces ("petiole_length/PETIlng" becomes "petiole length"); columns already renamed to codes are shown as they are.


Arguments







Argument
Description




analysis_data
A data frame produced by morph_matrix_setting(), with specimen identifiers as row names and the "base_cols" attribute. Do not strip attributes (e.g. by subsetting or rebuilding the data frame) before calling this function.


geodata
A data frame produced by geo_matrix_setting(), with specimen identifiers as row names and the decimalLatitude and decimalLongitude columns. Required when order_by is "latitude" or "longitude"; ignored when order_by = "none". Default is NULL.


blocks
Character vector of blocks to analyze. "all" (default) runs every available block and every combination of blocks. Otherwise, one or more of "veg", "flo", "fru", "vegflo", "vegfru", "flofru", and "vegflofru", restricted to the blocks available in analysis_data. Unavailable names are ignored with a warning.


cor_method
Character string giving the correlation coefficient used for the lag-1 autocorrelation. One of "pearson" (default), "spearman", or "kendall". Passed to stats::cor().


order_by
Character string giving how specimens are ordered before computing the autocorrelation. One of "latitude" (default), "longitude", or "none" (keep the row order of analysis_data).


file_formats
Character vector specifying the file formats used to save the charts. One or more of "pdf" and "jpg". Default is c("pdf", "jpg").


verbose
Logical. If TRUE (default), prints progress messages and, for each block, the number of traits computed and the traits with the highest and lowest autocorrelation.





Value
A list, returned invisibly, with the elements:
resultsA data frame with one row per trait and block, with columns block, trait, and autocor, or NULL if no block produced results. plotsA named list of ggplot2::ggplot() objects, one per block. specimen_orderCharacter vector of specimen identifiers in the order used. output_dirPath of the folder where the charts and the summary table were saved.
The function is also called for its side effects: charts and the summary table are written to output_dir.


Examples
# Both matrices must be built from the same specimens
geo <- geo_matrix_setting(
  xlsx_path = "specimen_data.xlsx",
  taxon_col = "species",
  edaphic = FALSE
)

morph <- morph_matrix_setting(
  xlsx_path = "specimen_data.xlsx",
  taxon_col = "species",
  trait_name_type = "code",
  veg_first = "petiole_length/PETIlng",
  flo_first = "inflorescence_length/INFLlng",
  fru_first = "fruit_stipe_length/FRSTlng"
)

# Every block and block combination, specimens ordered by latitude
res <- morph_autocorrelation(analysis_data = morph, geodata = geo)
head(res$results)

# Floral traits only, ordered by longitude, Spearman correlation
res <- morph_autocorrelation(
  analysis_data = morph,
  geodata = geo,
  blocks = "flo",
  cor_method = "spearman",
  order_by = "longitude"
)

# Keep the original spreadsheet order (geodata not needed)
res <- morph_autocorrelation(
  analysis_data = morph,
  blocks = c("veg", "fru"),
  order_by = "none",
  file_formats = "pdf"
)

title: morph_anova
text:
moRphoTaxa::morph_anova()


Description
Runs a one-way ANOVA for every morphological trait in each requested trait block, testing whether trait means differ across the levels of one or more grouping variables, and generates a summary bar plot and spreadsheet for each block x group combination. The function is designed to work directly on the objects produced by morph_matrix_setting().
For each trait block and each grouping variable, the function fits trait ~ group with stats::aov() for every trait in the block, collects the F statistic and p-value, adjusts p-values for multiple testing across the traits tested in that block, and saves a horizontal bar plot of F statistics (coloured by significance) together with a spreadsheet of the results.


Details
morph_anova() expects analysis_data as produced by morph_matrix_setting(): a numeric data frame with id and taxon columns plus one column per morphological trait, with specimen IDs as row names. The trait blocks ("veg", "flo", "fru", or any subset thereof) are not passed in separately — they are read directly from the "base_cols" attribute that morph_matrix_setting() attaches to analysis_data. If analysis_data has no "base_cols" attribute (e.g. it was not built with morph_matrix_setting(), or the attribute was dropped by an intervening subsetting operation), the function stops with an informative error.
Grouping variables are read from columns of analysis_data itself, named in anova_groups — by default just "taxon", the grouping column that morph_matrix_setting() always attaches. Passing any other name only works if that column has been added to analysis_data beforehand (e.g. a locality or growth-form column merged in before calling this function); morph_anova() does not read from any other object.
The anova_blocks argument controls which trait sets are analyzed:

"all": runs ANOVA on each individual block in base_cols (typically "veg", "flo", "fru"), as well as on every pairwise and full combination of these blocks ("vegflo", "vegfru", "flofru", "vegflofru"). Combinations whose source blocks are absent from base_cols are silently skipped;
a character vector naming one or more blocks in base_cols: runs ANOVA only on the requested block(s), individually.

Within each block x group combination, specimens with a missing value for the grouping variable are removed; the combination is skipped with a warning if fewer than 3 specimens or fewer than 2 group levels remain. Each trait is then tested individually: rows with a missing value for that particular trait or the grouping variable are omitted by stats::aov()’s default na.action, and a trait is skipped (silently, since this is expected for traits scored only in part of a block) if it has fewer than 3 non-missing values. A trait whose model fails to fit — for instance because it is constant within every group — is also skipped, since no F statistic exists in that case. This is an omnibus per-trait test: it indicates whether group means differ but does not identify which pairs of groups drive that difference; TukeyHSD or another post-hoc procedure can be run on the individual aov fits if that is needed.
P-values are adjusted with stats::p.adjust() using anova_p_adjust, separately within each block x group combination — that is, the correction accounts for the number of traits tested in that block, not for the total number of tests across all blocks and groups in the call. A trait is flagged significant when its adjusted p-value is below anova_alpha.
Output files are written to a date-specific directory inside Figs.ANOVA. For each block x group combination, a bar plot of F statistics (traits sorted from highest to lowest, coloured by significance, with a reference line at F = 1) is saved in the formats specified by file_formats, named "ANOVA_<block>_<group>". When save_xlsx = TRUE, a spreadsheet with that combination’s results is written alongside it, and a single "ANOVA_all_results.xlsx" combining every block x group combination is written once all combinations have been processed.


Arguments







Argument
Description




analysis_data
A numeric data frame containing morphological traits as columns and specimens as rows, with id and taxon columns and specimen identifiers as row names. Typically the object returned by morph_matrix_setting().


anova_blocks
Character. Either "all", to test every individual block in base_cols plus all pairwise and full combinations of these blocks, or a character vector naming one or more blocks in base_cols to test individually. Default is "all".


anova_groups
Character vector of column names in analysis_data to use as grouping variables, one ANOVA run per name. Default is "taxon".


anova_p_adjust
Character. Method passed to stats::p.adjust() for correcting p-values across the traits tested within each block x group combination. One of "bonferroni", "holm", "hochberg", "hommel", "BH" (default), "BY", or "none".


anova_alpha
Numeric between 0 and 1. Adjusted-p-value threshold below which a trait is flagged as significant. Default is 0.05.


save_xlsx
Logical. If TRUE (default), writes a spreadsheet of results for each block x group combination, plus a combined spreadsheet of every combination, to the output directory.


file_formats
Character vector specifying which image formats to save. One or more of "pdf" and "jpeg". Default is c("pdf", "jpeg").


verbose
Logical. If TRUE (default), prints progress messages, per-combination counts of traits tested and found significant, skipped combinations, and the output directory to the console.





Value
Invisibly returns a data frame combining the results of every analyzed block x group combination, or NULL if none could be analyzed. The columns are:
traitName of the morphological trait. F_statisticF statistic of the one-way ANOVA for that trait. p_valueUnadjusted p-value. p_adjustedP-value adjusted with anova_p_adjust, within the block x group combination. significant``TRUE when p_adjusted < anova_alpha. blockName of the trait block. groupName of the grouping variable.
The function is also called for its side effects: bar plots and (when save_xlsx = TRUE) spreadsheets of results are written to disk for each analyzed block x group combination.


Examples
# Build the morphometric matrix
res <- morph_matrix_setting(
  xlsx_path = "output_data/all_data.xlsx",
  taxon_col = "taxon",
  trait_name_type = "code",
  veg_first = "petiole_length/PETIlng",
  flo_first = "inflorescence_length/INFLlng",
  fru_first = "fruit_stipe_length/FRSTlng"
)

# Test every individual block and every block combination against taxon
anova_res <- morph_anova(
  analysis_data = res,
  anova_blocks = "all"
)

# Traits that differ significantly among taxa
subset(anova_res, significant)

# Vegetative block only, with a stricter correction
morph_anova(
  analysis_data = res,
  anova_blocks = "veg",
  anova_p_adjust = "bonferroni"
)

# Against a custom grouping column added beforehand
res$locality <- specimen_localities[rownames(res)]
morph_anova(
  analysis_data = res,
  anova_groups = "locality"
)

title: morph_dapc
text:
moRphoTaxa::morph_dapc()


Description
Performs a discriminant analysis of principal components (DAPC), via stats::prcomp() followed by adegenet::dapc(), on morphological trait blocks derived from a morphometric matrix, and generates a standard set of diagnostic figures and spreadsheets for each trait block analyzed. The function is designed to work directly on the objects produced by morph_matrix_setting().
For each requested trait block, the function fits a PCA on the scaled morphological traits, retains a subset of principal components, runs adegenet::dapc() on the retained components using taxon as the grouping variable, saves a discriminant-scores scatterplot (LD1 x LD2) with confidence ellipses per taxon, saves a membership-probability barplot showing each specimen’s assignment probability to every taxon, and saves an Excel workbook with the posterior membership probabilities and discriminant scores.


Details
morph_dapc() expects analysis_data as produced by morph_matrix_setting(): a numeric data frame with id and taxon columns plus one column per morphological trait, with specimen IDs as row names. The trait blocks ("veg", "flo", "fru", or any subset thereof) are not passed in separately — they are read directly from the "base_cols" attribute that morph_matrix_setting() attaches to analysis_data. If analysis_data has no "base_cols" attribute (e.g. it was not built with morph_matrix_setting(), or the attribute was dropped by an intervening subsetting operation), the function stops with an informative error.
The dapc_blocks argument controls which trait sets are analyzed:

"all": runs DAPC on each individual block in base_cols (typically "veg", "flo", "fru"), as well as on every pairwise and full combination of these blocks ("vegflo", "vegfru", "flofru", "vegflofru");
a character vector naming one or more blocks in base_cols: runs DAPC only on the requested block(s), individually.

For each trait block, the grouping variable is the taxon column of analysis_data. Rows with a missing taxon are dropped, and any taxon with fewer than dapc_min_n specimens (after that step) is removed from the block entirely, with a message identifying the removed taxa. Blocks left with fewer than 2 taxa are skipped with a warning.
Within each retained block, missing trait values are imputed with the column mean, and any trait with zero variance is dropped. A block is skipped, with a warning, if fewer than 2 traits remain, or if the number of specimens does not exceed the number of taxa. Remaining traits are centred and scaled (base::scale()) before a principal component analysis is fit with stats::prcomp() (scale. = FALSE, since the traits are already scaled).
The number of principal components retained for the discriminant step is controlled by dapc_n_pca: if NULL (default), the smallest number of components explaining at least 80% of the cumulative variance is used (with a minimum of 2 and a maximum of nrow - 1); otherwise the supplied value is used, capped at the number of components available. The number of discriminant functions is controlled by dapc_n_da: if NULL (default), n_groups - 1 is used (the maximum possible); otherwise the supplied value is used, capped at n_groups - 1. Discriminant functions are then fit with adegenet::dapc() on the retained principal components.
Taxon colours are taken from the "taxon_colors" attribute attached to analysis_data by morph_matrix_setting(), so that each taxon keeps the same colour used in other plots (e.g. morph_pca(), morph_cva(), morph_boxplots()). If this attribute is missing, or lacks an entry for a taxon retained in a given block, colours are generated automatically from the viridis palette for the affected taxa, with a warning.
Output files are written to a date-specific directory inside Figs_DAPC. For each analyzed block, the following files are generated:

a discriminant-scores scatterplot (LD1 x LD2, or LD1 alone if only one discriminant function is available), with a normal confidence ellipse per taxon at level dapc_ellipse ("DAPC_scatter_" prefix);
a membership-probability barplot, with one panel per taxon and one bar per specimen, showing the posterior probability of assignment to each taxon ("DAPC_membership_" prefix);
an Excel workbook with the posterior membership probabilities and discriminant scores ("DAPC_" prefix, .xlsx).

Plots are saved in the formats specified by file_formats. Once every requested block has been processed, a "DAPC_summary.xlsx" file collecting one row per successfully analyzed block is written to the same output directory.


Arguments







Argument
Description




analysis_data
A numeric data frame containing morphological traits as columns and specimens as rows, with id and taxon columns and specimen identifiers as row names. Typically the analysis_data element returned by morph_matrix_setting(). If this object carries a "taxon_colors" attribute, those colours are reused; otherwise a viridis palette is generated automatically.


dapc_blocks
Character. Either "all", to run DAPC on every individual block in base_cols plus all pairwise and full combinations of these blocks, or a character vector naming one or more blocks in base_cols to analyze individually. Default is "all".


dapc_n_pca
Integer or NULL. Number of principal components to retain before the discriminant step. If NULL (default), the number of components needed to explain at least 80% of the cumulative variance is used automatically for each block.


dapc_n_da
Integer or NULL. Number of discriminant functions to retain. If NULL (default), n_groups - 1 is used for each block (the maximum possible number of discriminant axes).


dapc_min_n
Integer. Minimum number of specimens a taxon must have, within a given trait block, to be retained in the DAPC for that block. Taxa with fewer specimens are dropped block-by-block. Default is 3.


dapc_ellipse
Numeric. Confidence level (between 0 and 1) used for the per-taxon normal confidence ellipses drawn on the discriminant-scores scatterplot. Default is 0.95.


file_formats
Character vector specifying which image formats to save. One or more of "pdf" and "jpeg". Default is c("pdf", "jpeg").


verbose
Logical. If TRUE (default), prints progress messages, including removed taxa, skipped blocks, retained components, and the output directory, to the console.





Value
Invisibly returns a data frame summarizing the blocks successfully analyzed, with one row per block and columns block, n, n_groups, n_pca, and n_da; or invisibly returns NULL if no block could be analyzed.
The function is primarily called for its side effects: discriminant-score scatterplots, membership-probability barplots, and per-block and summary Excel workbooks are written to disk for each analyzed trait block.


Examples
# Build the morphometric matrix
res <- morph_matrix_setting(
  xlsx_path = "output_data/all_data.xlsx",
  taxon_col = "taxon",
  trait_name_type = "code",
  veg_first = "petiole_length/PETIlng",
  flo_first = "inflorescence_length/INFLlng",
  fru_first = "fruit_stipe_length/FRSTlng"
)

# Run DAPC on every individual block and every block combination
morph_dapc(
  analysis_data = res,
  dapc_blocks = "all"
)

# Run DAPC on the vegetative block only, retaining 5 PCs
morph_dapc(
  analysis_data = res,
  dapc_blocks = "veg",
  dapc_n_pca = 5
)

# Run DAPC on selected blocks, requiring at least 5 specimens per taxon,
# saving PDF output only
morph_dapc(
  analysis_data = res,
  dapc_blocks = c("veg", "flo"),
  dapc_min_n = 5,
  file_formats = "pdf"
)

title: geo_morph_mantel
text:
moRphoTaxa::geo_morph_mantel()


Description
Tests whether morphological dissimilarity among specimens is correlated with the geographic distance between the localities where they were collected (isolation by distance), using a Mantel test.
Takes the geographical matrix produced by geo_matrix_setting() and the morphometric matrix produced by morph_matrix_setting(), matches specimens by their identifiers, computes one geographic and one morphological distance matrix, runs vegan::mantel(), prints a summary of the result, and draws a scatter plot of pairwise morphological versus geographic distances with a linear trend line.


Details
Matching specimens. Specimens are matched by row names. Both geo_matrix_setting() and morph_matrix_setting() use the specimen identifier (an existing "id" column, or automatic identifiers "ID0001", "ID0002", …) as row names, so the two matrices must be built from the same specimens (typically the same spreadsheet, or spreadsheets sharing an "id" column). Only specimens present in both matrices, with valid coordinates and at least one morphological measurement, are used. Specimens present in only one of the two matrices are ignored.
Morphological matrix. The "taxon" column of analysis_data is not part of the morphological distance. Only the numeric trait columns are used, and traits with no observation among the retained specimens are dropped.
Geographic distance. With geo_dist_method = "haversine" (default), pairwise great-circle distances are computed from decimalLatitude and decimalLongitude on a sphere of radius 6371.0088 km, and are expressed in kilometres. With "euclidean", the Euclidean distance between coordinates in decimal degrees is used instead; this is a rough approximation that distorts distances away from the equator and across wide longitudinal ranges.
Morphological distance.

"gower" (default): computed with cluster::daisy(). Each trait is range-standardized and the dissimilarity between two specimens is averaged over the traits measured in both, so missing values are handled pairwise: no specimen is dropped and nothing is imputed. An error is raised if some pair of specimens shares no measured trait.
"bray", "jaccard", "euclidean", "manhattan": computed with vegan::vegdist(). These methods require complete data, so specimens with any missing trait value are dropped (with a warning). Traits are used as they are, without any standardization, so traits measured on larger numeric scales dominate "euclidean" and "manhattan" distances; "bray" and "jaccard" additionally assume non-negative values.

Mantel test. The significance of the correlation is assessed by permuting the rows and columns of one distance matrix, so it accounts for the non-independence among pairwise distances. The linear trend line in the plot is purely descriptive and its confidence band should not be interpreted as a test. Because the permutations are random, call set.seed() before this function to obtain reproducible p-values.
Outputs. The plot is saved in a dated subfolder (format(Sys.time(), "%d%b%Y")) inside "Figs_Mantel", in the formats selected by file_formats. The dated subfolder means repeated runs do not overwrite each other.


Arguments







Argument
Description




geodata
A data frame produced by geo_matrix_setting(). It must contain the decimalLatitude and decimalLongitude columns, and its row names must be the specimen identifiers.


analysis_data
A data frame produced by morph_matrix_setting(). Its row names must be the specimen identifiers, and it must contain the numeric trait columns (a "taxon" column, if present, is ignored).


cor_method
Character string giving the correlation coefficient computed between the two distance matrices. One of "pearson" (default), "spearman", or "kendall". Passed to the method argument of vegan::mantel().


permutations
Integer. Number of permutations used to assess significance. Default is 999.


dist_method
Character string giving the morphological distance. One of "gower" (default), "bray", "jaccard", "euclidean", or "manhattan". See Details.


geo_dist_method
Character string giving the geographic distance. One of "haversine" (default; great-circle distance in km) or "euclidean" (Euclidean distance in decimal degrees). See Details.


file_formats
Character vector specifying the file formats used to save the plot. One or more of "pdf" and "jpg". Default is c("pdf", "jpg").


verbose
Logical. If TRUE (default), prints progress messages and a summary of the Mantel test results.





Value
A list, returned invisibly, with the elements:
mantelThe vegan::mantel() result (class "mantel"), including the Mantel statistic ($statistic) and the permutational p-value ($signif). dist_geoThe geographic distance matrix (class "dist"). dist_morphoThe morphological distance matrix (class "dist"). plotThe ggplot2::ggplot() object of the scatter plot. nNumber of specimens used in the test. output_dirPath of the folder where the plot was saved.
The function is also called for its side effects: the plot is written to output_dir and, when verbose = TRUE, a summary is printed to the console.


Examples
# Both matrices must be built from the same specimens
geo <- geo_matrix_setting(
  xlsx_path = "specimen_data.xlsx",
  taxon_col = "species",
  edaphic = FALSE
)

morph <- morph_matrix_setting(
  xlsx_path = "specimen_data.xlsx",
  taxon_col = "species",
  trait_name_type = "code",
  veg_first = "petiole_length/PETIlng",
  flo_first = "inflorescence_length/INFLlng",
  fru_first = "fruit_stipe_length/FRSTlng"
)

# Default: Pearson correlation, 999 permutations, Gower distance
set.seed(123)
res <- geo_morph_mantel(geodata = geo, analysis_data = morph)
res$mantel

# Rank correlation, more permutations, PDF only
res <- geo_morph_mantel(
  geodata = geo,
  analysis_data = morph,
  cor_method = "spearman",
  permutations = 9999,
  file_formats = "pdf"
)

# Complete-case Euclidean morphological distance, as in earlier scripts
# that used decimal degrees for the geographic distance
res <- geo_morph_mantel(
  geodata = geo,
  analysis_data = morph,
  dist_method = "euclidean",
  geo_dist_method = "euclidean"
)

title: morph_pcoa
text:
moRphoTaxa::morph_pcoa()


Description
Performs principal coordinates analysis (PCoA) on morphological trait blocks derived from a morphometric matrix, and generates a standard set of diagnostic figures for each trait block analyzed. The function is designed to work directly on the objects produced by morph_matrix_setting(), and mirrors the structure of morph_pca().
For each requested trait block, the function computes a specimen-by-specimen distance matrix, fits a PCoA, saves an ordination biplot with marginal density panels and vectors for the traits most correlated with the first two axes, saves a barplot of the correlation of the top traits with each of these axes, saves a barplot of the variation explained by the first axes, and, when at least three axes are available, saves a panel of pairwise scatterplots (PCo1 x PCo2, PCo1 x PCo3, PCo2 x PCo3).


Details
morph_pcoa() expects analysis_data as produced by morph_matrix_setting(): a numeric data frame with id and taxon columns plus one column per morphological trait, with specimen IDs as row names. The trait blocks ("veg", "flo", "fru", or any subset thereof) are not passed in separately: they are read directly from the "base_cols" attribute that morph_matrix_setting() attaches to analysis_data. If analysis_data has no "base_cols" attribute (e.g. it was not built with morph_matrix_setting(), or the attribute was dropped by an intervening subsetting operation), the function stops with an informative error.
The pcoa_blocks argument controls which trait sets are analyzed:

"all": runs PCoA on each individual block in base_cols (typically "veg", "flo", "fru"), as well as on every pairwise and full combination of these blocks ("vegflo", "vegfru", "flofru", "vegflofru");
a character vector naming one or more blocks in base_cols: runs PCoA only on the requested block(s), individually.

For each trait block, rows with missing values in the relevant columns are removed via stats::na.omit(), and traits with zero variance are dropped. Blocks with fewer than 3 specimens or fewer than 2 traits after this filtering, or with fewer than 2 ordination axes, are skipped with a warning.
Distance. The distance between specimens is set by dist_method:

"gower" (default): Gower distance for continuous traits, i.e. the mean, over traits, of the absolute difference between two specimens divided by the range of the trait. All traits have the same weight regardless of their units;
"euclidean": Euclidean distance on centred and scaled traits. The resulting PCoA is equivalent to the PCA computed by morph_pca().

Ordination. The PCoA is computed with ape::pcoa(). Distances such as Gower’s are not always Euclidean, in which case some eigenvalues are negative. correction controls how this is handled: "none" (default) uses only the axes with positive eigenvalues; "lingoes" and "cailliez" apply the corresponding additive-constant corrections. The percentage of variation shown on each axis is its eigenvalue divided by the sum of the positive eigenvalues (corrected eigenvalues when a correction is used). When negative eigenvalues are present and correction = "none", a message reports their magnitude.
Traits. PCoA is computed from distances, so it has no trait loadings of its own. As in the usual PCoA biplot, each trait is instead correlated (stats::cor()) with the ordination axes: the vectors in the biplot are drawn for the top_vars traits with the highest squared correlation with PCo1 and PCo2 combined, with lengths proportional to the correlations; and the two barplots show the correlation of the top_vars traits most correlated with PCo1 and with PCo2, respectively.
Taxon colours are taken from the "taxon_colors" attribute attached to analysis_data by morph_matrix_setting(), so that each taxon keeps the same colour used in other plots (e.g. morph_pca(), morph_dapc()). If this attribute is missing, or lacks an entry for a taxon present in a given block, colours are generated automatically from the viridis palette for the affected taxa, with a warning.
For each analyzed block, the following figures are generated:

a PCoA biplot (specimens and trait vectors) with marginal density panels along each axis, one density per taxon;
a barplot of the correlation of the top traits with PCo1;
a barplot of the correlation of the top traits with PCo2;
a barplot of the percentage of variation explained by the first (up to 10) axes;
when at least 3 axes are available, a three-panel figure with PCo1 x PCo2, PCo1 x PCo3, and PCo2 x PCo3 scatterplots.

Output files are written to a date-specific directory inside Figs.PCoA. Each figure is saved in the formats specified by file_formats. File names are prefixed by figure type ("PCoA_", "Dim1_corr_variables_", "Dim2_corr_variables_", "PCoA_eigenvalues_", "PCoA_panels_") and suffixed by the trait block name.


Arguments







Argument
Description




analysis_data
A numeric data frame containing morphological traits as columns and specimens as rows, with id and taxon columns and specimen identifiers as row names. Typically the analysis_data element returned by morph_matrix_setting(). If this object carries a "taxon_colors" attribute, those colours are reused; otherwise a viridis palette is generated automatically.


pcoa_blocks
Character. Either "all", to run PCoA on every individual block in base_cols plus all pairwise and full combinations of these blocks, or a character vector naming one or more blocks in base_cols to analyze individually. Default is "all".


dist_method
Character. Distance between specimens: "gower" (default) or "euclidean" (on scaled traits). See Details.


correction
Character. Correction for negative eigenvalues: "none" (default), "lingoes" or "cailliez". See Details.


top_vars
Integer. Number of traits shown as vectors in the biplot and as bars in the trait-correlation plots for PCo1 and PCo2. Default is 10.


file_formats
Character vector specifying which image formats to save. One or more of "pdf" and "jpeg". Default is c("pdf", "jpeg").


verbose
Logical. If TRUE (default), prints progress messages, including skipped blocks, negative eigenvalues and the output directory, to the console.





Value
Invisibly returns a named list with one element per analyzed block. Each element is a list with:
scoresA data frame with the ordination coordinates of each specimen (PCo1, PCo2, …) and its taxon, with specimen IDs as row names. eigenvaluesA data frame with the axis, eigenvalue and relative (proportion of the sum of positive eigenvalues) of each axis. n_specimens, n_traitsNumber of specimens and traits used.
The list is empty if no block could be analyzed.
The function is primarily called for its side effects: PCoA biplots, trait-correlation plots, eigenvalue plots and (when applicable) pairwise axis scatterplot panels are written to disk for each analyzed trait block.


Examples
# Build the morphometric matrix
res <- morph_matrix_setting(
  xlsx_path = "output_data/all_data.xlsx",
  taxon_col = "taxon",
  trait_name_type = "code",
  veg_first = "petiole_length/PETIlng",
  flo_first = "inflorescence_length/INFLlng",
  fru_first = "fruit_stipe_length/FRSTlng"
)

# Run PCoA (Gower distance) on every individual block and every combination
morph_pcoa(
  analysis_data = res,
  pcoa_blocks = "all"
)

# Vegetative block only, with a Lingoes correction for negative eigenvalues
morph_pcoa(
  analysis_data = res,
  pcoa_blocks = "veg",
  correction = "lingoes"
)

# Selected blocks, Euclidean distance on scaled traits, top 15 traits,
# saving PDF output only
pco <- morph_pcoa(
  analysis_data = res,
  pcoa_blocks = c("veg", "flo"),
  dist_method = "euclidean",
  top_vars = 15,
  file_formats = "pdf"
)

# Ordination coordinates of the vegetative block
head(pco$veg$scores)

title: morph_dendrogram
text:
moRphoTaxa::morph_dendrogram()


Description
Builds hierarchical clustering dendrograms for morphological trait blocks derived from a morphometric matrix, with automated selection of the linkage method and number of clusters, and generates diagnostic and dendrogram figures for each trait block analyzed. The function is designed to work directly on the objects produced by morph_matrix_setting().


Details
morph_dendrogram() expects analysis_data as produced by morph_matrix_setting(): a numeric data frame with id and taxon columns plus one column per morphological trait, with specimen IDs as row names. The trait blocks ("veg", "flo", "fru", or any subset thereof) are not passed in separately — they are read directly from the "base_cols" attribute that morph_matrix_setting() attaches to analysis_data. If analysis_data has no "base_cols" attribute, the function stops with an informative error.
The dendro_blocks argument controls which trait sets are analyzed:

"all": runs the analysis on each individual block in base_cols (typically "veg", "flo", "fru"), as well as on every pairwise and full combination of these blocks ("vegflo", "vegfru", "flofru", "vegflofru") that can be fully built from the blocks present;
a character vector naming one or more blocks in base_cols: runs the analysis only on the requested block(s), individually.

For each trait block, rows with missing values in the block’s columns are removed via stats::na.omit(). Blocks with fewer than 3 remaining specimens or fewer than 2 traits are skipped with a warning.
When a block has more than 2 traits, the traits used for clustering are first narrowed to those contributing more than the average expected contribution to PC1 (100 / p, where p is the number of traits in the block) — the same reference-line criterion used by factoextra::fviz_contrib() to flag “significant” variables. If fewer than 2 traits pass this criterion, the top 2 contributing traits are used instead, so that at least 2 traits are always retained for clustering.
A distance matrix is computed on the retained traits with vegan::vegdist() using dist_method. Each of linkage_candidates is fit with stats::hclust(), and the linkage whose cophenetic distances correlate best with the original distance matrix (Sokal & Rohlf’s cophenetic correlation) is selected automatically. The number of clusters k is then chosen automatically, from 2 up to min(k_max, n - 1), as the value maximizing the average silhouette width (cluster::silhouette()).
For each analyzed block, the function produces:

a bar plot of cophenetic correlation by candidate linkage method;
a line plot of average silhouette width by candidate k, with the selected k marked;
a vertical dendrogram, with branches colored by the statistical cluster assignment (k groups) and leaf labels colored by known taxon, so the two can be visually compared;
a horizontal version of the same dendrogram.

Diagnostic plots are saved in the formats specified by file_formats. Dendrograms are base-R plots and are always saved as both PDF and JPEG, since file_formats controls ggplot2::ggplot()-based diagnostic output only.
Leaf labels in each dendrogram are colored by known taxon. These taxon colours are taken from the "taxon_colors" attribute attached to analysis_data by morph_matrix_setting(), so that each taxon keeps the same colour used in other plots (e.g. morph_boxplots(), morph_pca()). If this attribute is missing, or lacks an entry for a taxon present in a given block, colours are generated automatically from the viridis palette for the affected taxa, with a warning. This is independent of cluster_cols, which colors the dendrogram branches by statistical cluster rather than by taxon.
Output files are written to a date-specific directory inside Figs.dendrogram.


Arguments







Argument
Description




analysis_data
A numeric data frame containing morphological traits as columns and specimens as rows, with id and taxon columns and specimen identifiers as row names. Typically the output of morph_matrix_setting(). If this object carries a "taxon_colors" attribute, those colours are reused for the taxon leaf labels; otherwise a viridis palette is generated automatically.


dendro_blocks
Character. Either "all", to run the analysis on every individual block in base_cols plus all pairwise and full combinations of these blocks, or a character vector naming one or more blocks in base_cols to analyze individually. Default is "all".


dist_method
Character string giving the distance method passed to vegan::vegdist() (e.g. "bray", "jaccard", "euclidean", "manhattan", "gower"). Default is "bray".


linkage_candidates
Character vector of linkage methods to compare, passed in turn to stats::hclust(). Default is c("complete", "average", "ward.D2", "single").


k_max
Integer. Upper bound for the number of clusters considered during the silhouette-width search. Automatically capped at n - 1 for each trait block. Default is 8.


cluster_cols
Character vector of colors used for dendrogram branches, one per cluster. If NULL (default), a palette is generated automatically for each block, sized exactly to that block’s selected number of clusters (best_k), so clusters are never forced to repeat colors. If a vector is supplied, it is recycled when the selected number of clusters exceeds its length — a warning is issued if this happens, since repeated colors can make distinct clusters visually indistinguishable. This controls branch colours only — leaf-label colours by taxon come from analysis_data’s "taxon_colors" attribute (see Details).


file_formats
Character vector specifying which image formats to save the ggplot-based diagnostic plots in. One or more of "pdf" and "jpeg". Default is c("pdf", "jpeg"). Dendrograms themselves are always saved as both PDF and JPEG.


verbose
Logical. If TRUE (default), prints progress messages, including skipped blocks, selected linkage/k, and the output directory, to the console.





Value
Invisibly returns NULL.
The function is primarily called for its side effects: diagnostic plots and vertical/horizontal dendrograms are written to disk for each analyzed trait block.


Examples
# Build the morphometric matrix
res <- morph_matrix_setting(
  xlsx_path = "output_data/all_data.xlsx",
  taxon_col = "taxon",
  trait_name_type = "code",
  veg_first = "petiole_length/PETIlng",
  flo_first = "inflorescence_length/INFLlng",
  fru_first = "fruit_stipe_length/FRSTlng"
)

# Dendrograms for every individual block and every block combination
morph_dendrogram(analysis_data = res, dendro_blocks = "all")

# Dendrogram for the vegetative block only, using Euclidean distance
morph_dendrogram(
  analysis_data = res,
  dendro_blocks = "veg",
  dist_method = "euclidean"
)

title: morph_add_traits
text:
moRphoTaxa::morph_add_traits()


Description
Creates a standardized morphological trait matrix for morphometric analyses. The function can either append morphological trait columns to an existing specimen-occurrence data frame or create an empty trait matrix when base_df = NULL.
Trait columns can include a general set of qualitative and quantitative characters applicable across flowering plants, as well as additional taxon-specific characters selected from predefined morphological presets. Trait names may be returned as full descriptive names, abbreviated trait codes, or a combination of both.


Details
morph_add_traits() is intended to prepare standardized data matrices for downstream morphometric analyses in moRphoTaxa. The function distinguishes between two major classes of morphological characters:

Qualitative traits, such as leaf shape, indumentum, floral morphology, fruit type, and seed morphology.
Quantitative traits, such as lengths, widths, areas, numbers, and other measurements of vegetative and reproductive structures.

Default trait sets contain characters broadly applicable to flowering plants. Additional taxon-specific traits can be requested independently for qualitative and quantitative characters using quali_specific and quanti_specific.
